brief: Wiremu Te Tauri of Ngāti Tūwharetoa and Whanganui was for some time the head teacher for Richard Taylor. He was present at the tangi for the martyrs Te Manihera and Kereopa in 1847 and argued against utu. He said, “A minister was like a lofty kahikatea tree full of fruit, which it sheds on every side around, causing a thick grove of young trees to spring up; so that although the parent tree may be cut down, its place is thus more than supplied by those which proceed from it.”
